165	  if [[ "$do_scp" =~ ^[Yy] ]]; then
166	    local key_basename="${key_path##*/}"
167	    printf '\n> scp %s %s.pub %s:~/.ssh/\n' "$key_path" "$key_path" "$target"
168	    scp "$key_path" "${key_path}.pub" "$target:~/.ssh/" || return 1
169	    ssh "$target" "chmod 600 ~/.ssh/$key_basename && chmod 644 ~/.ssh/${key_basename}.pub"
170	    printf 'Key copied and permissions set.\n'
171	
172	    # Configure GitHub on remote
173	    printf '\nAdd GitHub SSH config on remote? [y/N] '
174	    local do_github
175	    read -r do_github
176	    if [[ "$do_github" =~ ^[Yy] ]]; then
177	      ssh "$target" "mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/config" <<EOF
178	
179	Host github.com
180	    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/$key_basename
181	EOF
182	      ssh "$target" "chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config"
183	      printf 'GitHub SSH config added on remote.\n'
184	    fi
185	  fi
186	
187	  # ── Step 3: Local SSH config ───────────────────────────────────────────
188	  printf '\n--- Local SSH config ---\n'
189	  printf 'Add host alias to local ~/.ssh/config? [Y/n] '
190	  local do_config
191	  read -r do_config
192	  if [[ ! "$do_config" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
193	    local host_alias="$remote_host"
194	    printf 'Host alias [%s]: ' "$host_alias"
195	    local alias_input
196	    read -r alias_input
197	    [ -n "$alias_input" ] && host_alias="$alias_input"
198	
199	    local hostname="$remote_host"
200	    printf 'HostName (IP or FQDN) [%s]: ' "$hostname"
201	    local hostname_input
202	    read -r hostname_input
203	    [ -n "$hostname_input" ] && hostname="$hostname_input"
204	
205	    local config_user="${remote_user:-$USER}"
206	    printf 'User [%s]: ' "$config_user"
207	    local user_input
208	    read -r user_input
209	    [ -n "$user_input" ] && config_user="$user_input"
210	
211	    printf 'Add IdentitiesOnly yes? [y/N] '
212	    local do_identonly
213	    read -r do_identonly
214	    local identonly_line=""
215	    [[ "$do_identonly" =~ ^[Yy] ]] && identonly_line=$'\n    IdentitiesOnly yes'
216	
217	    # Determine config file (support config.d/ if Include exists)
218	    local config_file="$HOME/.ssh/config"
219	    if [ -d "$HOME/.ssh/config.d" ]; then
220	      printf 'Write to ~/.ssh/config.d/ instead of ~/.ssh/config? [Y/n] '
221	      local use_configd
222	      read -r use_configd
223	      if [[ ! "$use_configd" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
224	        config_file="$HOME/.ssh/config.d/host_${host_alias}"
225	        printf 'Config file [%s]: ' "$config_file"
226	        local cf_input
227	        read -r cf_input
228	        [ -n "$cf_input" ] && config_file="$cf_input"
229	      fi
230	    fi
231	
232	    local config_block="
233	Host $host_alias
234	    HostName $hostname
235	    User $config_user
236	    IdentityFile $key_path${identonly_line}"
237	
238	    printf '\nWill append to %s:\n' "$config_file"
239	    printf '%s\n' "$config_block"
240	    printf '\nConfirm? [Y/n] '
241	    local confirm
242	    read -r confirm
243	    if [[ ! "$confirm" =~ ^[Nn] ]]; then
244	      printf '%s\n' "$config_block" >> "$config_file"
245	      chmod 600 "$config_file"
246	      printf 'Config written.\n'
247	    fi
248	  fi
249	
250	  # ── Done ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
251	  printf '\n=== Done! ===\n'
252	  printf 'Test with: ssh %s\n' "${host_alias:-$target}"
253	  if [[ "$do_scp" =~ ^[Yy] ]]; then

10	"""
11	dotfiles_init.py — Interactive wrapper around `chezmoi init` inspired by
12	Vercel Labs' `skills` CLI (https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
13	
14	The existing `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` defines the prompt set (profile, email,
15	name, feature flags, and preferences). `chezmoi init` asks them sequentially, which works but
16	hides the feature flags from each other and makes "set up a new machine
17	the way I always do" a manual checklist. This wrapper:
18	
19	  1. Pre-flights chezmoi / git / SSH key and offers to fix gaps.
20	  2. Lets you pick a pre-configured BUNDLE (personal-mac, work-mac,
21	     server-linux, minimal) that ticks typical feature flags for you.
22	  3. Presents feature flags grouped, as a questionary multi-select you can
23	     fly through with Space + Enter.
24	  4. Shells out to `chezmoi init <repo> --apply [--ssh] --promptString ... `
25	     so chezmoi remains the source of truth — we just pre-answer its prompts.
26	  5. Streams chezmoi's output live and prints a recap at the end.
27	
28	PROMPTS (below) is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The `gen` subcommand renders
29	the prompt block in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` and the ARG + flag blocks in
30	`Dockerfile` from it (between marker comments). `gen --check` (wired into
31	pre-commit) fails loudly if the on-disk files drift, so adding a prompt is
32	"edit PROMPTS, run `just gen-prompts`" rather than a manual three-file edit.
33	
34	Invocation:
35	    # Fresh machine (via bootstrap.sh which installs uv + chezmoi first):
36	    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash

39	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py
40

42	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen
43	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check
44	"""

96	@dataclass(frozen=True)
97	class When:
98	    """Declarative gate for a prompt — the decision-tree primitive.
99	
100	    Each dimension is a set of allowed values; an empty set means
101	    "unconstrained". Values WITHIN a dimension are OR'd, dimensions are
102	    AND'd together. The dimensions map onto chezmoi template facts:
103	
104	      - ``os``      -> ``.chezmoi.os``   ("darwin" / "linux")
105	      - ``arch``    -> ``.chezmoi.arch`` ("amd64" / "arm64")
106	      - ``profile`` -> the init-time ``$profile`` local (NOT ``.profile``,
107	                       which doesn't exist yet while .chezmoi.toml.tmpl renders)
108	
109	    A single ``When`` drives all three consumers (template conditional, TUI
110	    gating, Dockerfile is unconditional) so they can never disagree.
111	    """
112	    os: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
113	    profile: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
114	    arch: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
115	
116	    def matches(self, os_name: str, profile: object, arch: str) -> bool:
117	        if self.os and os_name not in self.os:
118	            return False
119	        if self.profile and profile not in self.profile:
120	            return False
121	        if self.arch and arch not in self.arch:
122	            return False
123	        return True
124	
125	    def to_go(self) -> str:
126	        """Render the Go-template boolean expression WITHOUT the surrounding
127	        ``{{ if }}`` — e.g. ``eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"`` or
128	        ``or (eq $profile "macos") (eq $profile "ubuntu_desktop")``."""
129	        dim_exprs: list[str] = []
130	        for var, values in (
131	            (".chezmoi.os", self.os),
132	            (".chezmoi.arch", self.arch),
133	            ("$profile", self.profile),
134	        ):
135	            if not values:
136	                continue
137	            eqs = ['eq %s "%s"' % (var, v) for v in sorted(values)]
138	            if len(eqs) == 1:
139	                dim_exprs.append(eqs[0])
140	            else:
141	                dim_exprs.append("or " + " ".join("(%s)" % e for e in eqs))
142	        if not dim_exprs:
143	            return ""
144	        if len(dim_exprs) == 1:
145	            return dim_exprs[0]
146	        return "and " + " ".join("(%s)" % e for e in dim_exprs)

543	@dataclass
544	class Preflight:
545	    chezmoi: str | None
546	    git: str | None
547	    ssh_hint: str | None                # how we detected SSH is ready (or None)
548	    source_exists: bool
549	    os_name: str
550	    arch: str                           # normalized to chezmoi's .chezmoi.arch (amd64/arm64)
551	    is_tty: bool
552	    chezmoi_is_snap: bool = False       # resolved chezmoi lives under /snap (see _resolve_chezmoi)
553	
554	
555	def _normalize_arch(machine: str) -> str:
556	    """Map platform.machine() onto chezmoi's GOARCH-style .chezmoi.arch."""
557	    return {
558	        "x86_64": "amd64", "amd64": "amd64",
559	        "aarch64": "arm64", "arm64": "arm64",
560	    }.get(machine.lower(), machine.lower())
561	
562	
563	def _prompt_applies(p: Prompt, os_name: str, profile: object, arch: str) -> bool:
564	    """True if `p` should be asked on this host (no condition = always)."""
565	    return p.condition is None or p.condition.matches(os_name, profile, arch)
566	
567	
568	def read_current_config() -> dict[str, object]:
569	    """Return the `[data]` table of ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml as a dict
570	    of {prompt_key: current_value}, or {} if the config doesn't exist / can't
571	    be parsed. This is what `reconfigure` seeds the TUI with so you toggle
572	    deltas from the live state instead of from prompt defaults."""
573	    if not CHEZMOI_CONFIG.exists():
574	        return {}
575	    try:
576	        return tomllib.loads(CHEZMOI_CONFIG.read_text()).get("data", {}) or {}
577	    except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
578	        return {}
579	
580	
581	def _detect_ssh() -> str | None:
582	    """Return a short hint describing why we think SSH-to-github is configured,
583	    or None if we can't tell. We accept several signals because the user may
584	    keep keys under non-canonical names and route them via ~/.ssh/config or
585	    its Include'd fragments."""
586	    # (1) Canonical default keys.
587	    for k in SSH_DEFAULT_KEYS:
588	        if k.exists():
589	            return f"default key at {k}"
590	    # (2) ~/.ssh/config (or an Include'd file under ~/.ssh/config.d/) with a
591	    # `Host github…` stanza → user is routing a custom key.
592	    config_texts: list[str] = []
593	    for root in (SSH_CONFIG, *((SSH_DIR / "config.d").glob("*") if (SSH_DIR / "config.d").is_dir() else ())):
594	        if root.is_file():
595	            try:
596	                config_texts.append(root.read_text(errors="replace"))
597	            except OSError:
598	                pass
599	    joined = "\n".join(config_texts)
600	    if re.search(r"(?mi)^\s*Host\s+[\w.\-\* ]*github", joined):
601	        return "~/.ssh/config routes github.com"
602	    # (3) Any loaded key in the agent (default or via IdentityAgent socket).
603	    try:
604	        r = subprocess.run(["ssh-add", "-l"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3)
605	        if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip():
606	            return "ssh-agent has keys loaded"
607	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
608	        pass
609	    return None
610	
611	
612	def detect() -> Preflight:
613	    import platform
614	    chezmoi_bin, is_snap = _resolve_chezmoi()
615	    return Preflight(
616	        chezmoi=chezmoi_bin,
617	        git=shutil.which("git"),
618	        ssh_hint=_detect_ssh(),
619	        source_exists=(CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR / ".git").is_dir(),
620	        os_name={"Darwin": "darwin", "Linux": "linux"}.get(platform.system(), platform.system().lower()),
621	        arch=_normalize_arch(platform.machine()),
622	        is_tty=sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty(),
623	        chezmoi_is_snap=is_snap,
624	    )
625

627	def print_preflight(pf: Preflight) -> None:
628	    t = Table(title="Preflight", show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
629	    t.add_column(); t.add_column()
630	    if pf.chezmoi and pf.chezmoi_is_snap:
631	        chezmoi_cell = f"⚠ [yellow]{pf.chezmoi} (snap — stdin/stdout bug; will install ~/.local/bin/chezmoi)[/yellow]"
632	    elif pf.chezmoi:
633	        chezmoi_cell = "✓ " + pf.chezmoi
634	    else:
635	        chezmoi_cell = "✗ [red]not found[/red]"
636	    t.add_row("chezmoi", chezmoi_cell)
637	    t.add_row("git", "✓ " + pf.git if pf.git else "✗ [red]not found[/red]")
638	    t.add_row("SSH", f"✓ {pf.ssh_hint}" if pf.ssh_hint else "✗ [yellow]no signal found[/yellow]")
639	    t.add_row("chezmoi source", "✓ present (re-init mode)" if pf.source_exists else "– fresh init")
640	    console.print(t)
641	    console.print()
642	
643	
644	def _resolve_chezmoi() -> tuple[str | None, bool]:
645	    """Resolve the chezmoi binary, preferring ~/.local/bin over a snap install.
646	
647	    The snap build of chezmoi has a long-standing stdin/stdout
648	    `permission denied` bug (chezmoi.io troubleshooting FAQ) that breaks this
649	    repo's modify_ / run_ scripts, and chezmoi upstream recommends installing
650	    via get.chezmoi.io instead. So we prefer ~/.local/bin/chezmoi, and when the
651	    only binary on PATH lives under /snap we flag it for replacement.
652	
653	    Returns (path or None, is_snap)."""
654	    local = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin" / "chezmoi"
655	    if local.exists():
656	        return str(local), False
657	    found = shutil.which("chezmoi")
658	    if not found:
659	        return None, False
660	    return found, found.startswith("/snap/") or "/snap/" in found
661	
662	
663	def install_chezmoi_interactive(os_name: str) -> str:
664	    """Offer to install chezmoi via the canonical one-liner; return new path."""
665	    if not questionary.confirm("chezmoi not found. Install via get.chezmoi.io/lb?", default=True).ask():
666	        console.print("[red]chezmoi is required; aborting.[/red]")
667	        sys.exit(1)
668	    target = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"
669	    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
670	    subprocess.check_call(
671	        "curl -fsLS --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 get.chezmoi.io/lb | sh",
672	        shell=True,
673	        env={**os.environ, "BINDIR": str(target)},
674	    )
675	    # Prefer the freshly-installed ~/.local/bin binary over any snap/brew one
676	    # that PATH might resolve first.
677	    local = target / "chezmoi"
678	    path = str(local) if local.exists() else (shutil.which("chezmoi") or str(local))
679	    console.print(f"[green]chezmoi installed at {path}[/green]\n")
680	    return path
681	
682	
683	def ensure_ssh_key_interactive() -> Path | None:
684	    """Offer to generate an ed25519 key; return path or None if user declined."""
685	    if not questionary.confirm(
686	        "No SSH key found. Generate ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 for GitHub (SSH clone)?",
687	        default=True,
688	    ).ask():
689	        return None
690	    key_path = Path.home() / ".ssh" / "id_ed25519"
691	    key_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
692	    email = questionary.text(
693	        "Email to tag the SSH key with:",
694	        default="daviddwlee84@gmail.com",
695	    ).ask() or "daviddwlee84@gmail.com"
696	    subprocess.check_call(["ssh-keygen", "-t", "ed25519", "-C", email, "-f", str(key_path), "-N", ""])
697	    pub = key_path.with_suffix(".pub").read_text().strip()
698	    console.print(Panel(
699	        f"[bold]Add this public key to GitHub → Settings → SSH keys:[/bold]\n\n{pub}\n\n"
700	        f"Open: https://github.com/settings/ssh/new",
701	        title="SSH key generated",
702	        border_style="green",
703	    ))
704	    questionary.press_any_key_to_continue("Press any key once you've added the key to GitHub...").ask()
705	    return key_path

712	def ask_bundle() -> str:
713	    choices = [
714	        questionary.Choice(
715	            title=f"{name:<14} — {summary}",
716	            value=name,
717	        )
718	        for name, summary in [
719	            ("personal-mac", "full personal setup (AI desktop apps, LLM tools, Brewfile)"),
720	            ("work-mac",     "safer: coding agents + dev tooling, no personal AI apps"),
721	            ("server-linux", "headless linux — coding agents, networking, dev tooling"),
722	            ("cloud-vm",     "lean throwaway VM — shell + tmux + nvim + coding agents only"),
723	            ("minimal",      "dotfiles only, no installX flags"),
724	            ("custom",       "no overrides — tick every feature yourself"),
725	        ]
726	    ]
727	    return questionary.select(
728	        "Pick a bundle:",
729	        choices=choices,
730	        default=choices[0],
731	    ).ask() or "custom"
732	
733	
734	def ask_basics(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
735	    # profile: auto-detect on Darwin; ask ubuntu_desktop vs ubuntu_server on Linux
736	    default_profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"
737	    if pf.os_name == "darwin":
738	        profile = "macos"
739	        console.print(f"[dim]profile → {profile} (auto-detected)[/dim]")
740	    else:
741	        # All non-macOS profile choices (keep server first as the common default).
742	        linux_choices = ["ubuntu_server", "ubuntu_desktop", "centos_server"]
743	        profile = questionary.select(
744	            "Which profile?",
745	            choices=linux_choices,
746	            default=overrides.get("profile", default_profile),
747	        ).ask() or default_profile
748	
749	    name = questionary.text(
750	        "Your full name:",
751	        default=str(overrides.get("name", _default_for("name"))),
752	    ).ask() or _default_for("name")
753	
754	    email = questionary.text(
755	        "Your git email:",
756	        default=str(overrides.get("email", _default_for("email"))),
757	    ).ask() or _default_for("email")
758	
759	    return {"profile": profile, "name": name, "email": email}
760	
761	
762	def resolve_basics_non_interactive(
763	    pf: Preflight,
764	    overrides: dict[str, object],
765	    *,
766	    name_flag: str | None,
767	    email_flag: str | None,
768	    profile_flag: str | None,
769	) -> dict[str, object]:
770	    """Non-interactive basics: flag → bundle override → embedded default → OS auto-detect."""
771	    if profile_flag:
772	        profile = profile_flag
773	    elif "profile" in overrides:
774	        profile = overrides["profile"]
775	    else:
776	        profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"

901	def build_chezmoi_argv(
902	    answers: dict[str, object],
903	    *,
904	    chezmoi_bin: str,
905	    repo: str | None,
906	    use_ssh: bool,
907	    apply: bool,
908	    prompt: bool = False,
909	) -> list[str]:
910	    """Build the chezmoi init argv. The critical detail is that `chezmoi init`
911	    matches --promptBool / --promptString / --promptChoice flags by the PROMPT
912	    TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce in the template), NOT the key name. That's
913	    why every Prompt carries a prompt_text field and we use it here as the
914	    flag key. We only emit flags for prompts present in `answers` (i.e. the
915	    ones applicable to this host); chezmoi harmlessly ignores extras anyway.
916	
917	    `prompt=True` adds `--prompt`, which FORCES the `prompt*Once` template
918	    functions to prompt again. This is mandatory when re-initializing an
919	    already-configured machine: without it, chezmoi reads the existing value
920	    from ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml's [data] and our --promptX flags are
921	    silently ignored (so the answers never actually change). With --prompt,
922	    every Once call re-fires and our flags satisfy them non-interactively."""
923	    argv: list[str] = [chezmoi_bin, "init"]
924	    if repo:
925	        argv.append(repo)
926	    if use_ssh:
927	        argv.append("--ssh")
928	    if apply:
929	        argv.append("--apply")
930	    if prompt:
931	        argv.append("--prompt")
932	    by_key = {p.key: p for p in PROMPTS}
933	    # String + choice prompts (basics).
934	    for key in ("email", "name"):
935	        if key in answers:
936	            argv += ["--promptString", f"{by_key[key].prompt_text}={answers[key]}"]
937	    if "profile" in answers:
938	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{by_key['profile'].prompt_text}={answers['profile']}"]
939	
940	    # Emit a flag for EVERY non-hidden prompt — not just the host-applicable
941	    # ones. Host-gated prompts whose `condition` doesn't match this machine are
942	    # absent from `answers`; we still pass their `else_value` so the flag set is
943	    # COMPLETE. This matters under --prompt (re-init / reconfigure), which
944	    # re-fires *all* promptXOnce: if the template's `$profile` ever differs from
945	    # the profile we resolved (e.g. a desktop→server migration mid-reconfigure),
946	    # a gated promptBoolOnce can still execute, and without a matching flag it
947	    # falls through to an interactive prompt mid-apply (the very leak this fixes:
948	    # `Install general GUI apps…?` / `Install Traditional Chinese IME?`). chezmoi
949	    # silently ignores any flag whose prompt the template never calls, so the
950	    # extra flags are harmless on hosts where the else-branch is baked instead.
951	    def _flag_value(p: Prompt) -> object | None:
952	        if p.key in answers:
953	            return answers[p.key]
954	        if p.condition is not None:        # gated-off here → bake else_value
955	            return p.else_value
956	        return None                        # applicable but unanswered → skip
957	
958	    # Non-basics choice prompts (e.g. discordChannel, backupMode, motdStyle).
959	    for p in PROMPTS:
960	        if p.kind != "choice" or p.hidden:
961	            continue
962	        val = _flag_value(p)
963	        if val is None:
964	            continue
965	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{p.prompt_text}={val}"]
966	    # Bool prompts.
967	    for p in PROMPTS:
968	        if p.kind != "bool" or p.hidden:
969	            continue
970	        val = _flag_value(p)
971	        if val is None:
972	            continue
973	        val_str = "true" if val else "false"
974	        argv += ["--promptBool", f"{p.prompt_text}={val_str}"]
975	    return argv
976

980	    console.rule("[bold]chezmoi output[/bold]")
981	    rc = subprocess.call(argv)
982	    console.rule()
983	    return rc

1014	DOCKER_ARGS_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:args <<<"
1015	DOCKER_RUN_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:init-run (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1016	DOCKER_RUN_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:init-run <<<"
1017	README_BEGIN = "<!-- dotfiles-init:prompts (coverage-checked by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check) -->"
1018	README_END = "<!-- /dotfiles-init:prompts -->"
1019	
1020	# Docker devbox build defaults — deliberately leaner than the prompt defaults
1021	# so the CI image builds fast (skip the heavy coding-agent / uv / js installs,
1022	# no backup). Anything not listed uses the prompt's own default.
1023	DOCKER_ARG_DEFAULTS: dict[str, object] = {

1039	def _key_to_arg(key: str) -> str:
1040	    """camelCase chezmoi key -> CHEZMOI_UPPER_SNAKE Docker ARG name."""
1041	    return "CHEZMOI_" + re.sub(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])", "_", key).upper()
1042	
1043	
1044	def _prompt_once_call(p: Prompt) -> str:
1045	    """The `{{ promptXOnce ... }}` assignment value for a prompt."""
1046	    if p.kind == "bool":
1047	        return "{{ promptBoolOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" %s }}" % (
1048	            p.key, p.prompt_text, "true" if p.default else "false")
1049	    if p.kind == "choice":
1050	        choices = " ".join('"%s"' % c for c in p.choices)
1051	        return "{{ promptChoiceOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" (list %s) \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1052	            p.key, p.prompt_text, choices, p.default)
1053	    return "{{ promptStringOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1054	        p.key, p.prompt_text, p.default)
1055	
1056	
1057	def _go_literal(kind: PromptType, value: object) -> str:
1058	    """Render an else_value as a TOML literal baked into the template."""
1059	    if kind == "bool":
1060	        return "true" if value else "false"
1061	    return '"%s"' % value
1062	
1063	
1064	def render_tmpl_body() -> str:
1065	    """Render the generated .chezmoi.toml.tmpl prompt block (non-hidden prompts)."""
1066	    lines: list[str] = []
1067	    for p in PROMPTS:
1068	        if p.hidden:
1069	            continue
1070	        for cl in p.comment.split("\n") if p.comment else []:
1071	            lines.append(("# " + cl).rstrip())
1072	        assign = "%s = %s" % (p.key, _prompt_once_call(p))
1073	        if p.condition is None:
1074	            lines.append(assign)
1075	        else:
1076	            lines.append("{{ if %s -}}" % p.condition.to_go())
1077	            lines.append(assign)
1078	            lines.append("{{ else -}}")
1079	            lines.append("%s = %s" % (p.key, _go_literal(p.kind, p.else_value)))
1080	            lines.append("{{ end -}}")
1081	    return "\n".join(lines)
1082

1090	        lines.append("ARG %s=%s" % (_key_to_arg(key), quoted))
1091	    for p in PROMPTS:

1095	        v_str = ("true" if v else "false") if p.kind == "bool" else str(v)
1096	        lines.append("ARG %s=%s" % (_key_to_arg(p.key), v_str))

1	# Config file conventions
2	
3	A quick tour of the dotfile / config organisation patterns this repo
4	uses, why each exists, and where to place new files.
5	
6	This is a **conventions reference**, not a chezmoi tutorial — for
7	chezmoi mechanics see [`tools/chezmoi-templating.md`](../tools/chezmoi-templating.md)
8	and [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). For
9	the shell-specific tier rule see
10	[`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## A. Where configs live
15	
16	### A1. XDG Base Directory Specification
17	
18	[freedesktop.org spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html);
19	the modern default. Four env vars carve up `$HOME` into purpose-tagged
20	subtrees:
21	
22	| Env var             | Default                | What goes there |
23	| ------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------- |
24	| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`  | `~/.config/`           | User config (this is where 90% of modern tools land) |
25	| `$XDG_DATA_HOME`    | `~/.local/share/`      | App data, tool installs (mise toolchains, oh-my-zsh, blesh, …) |
26	| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`   | `~/.cache/`            | Disposable caches (zsh history search cache, bat cache, …) |
27	| `$XDG_STATE_HOME`   | `~/.local/state/`      | Runtime state (less critical than data; used less often) |
28	| `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`  | `/run/user/$UID/`      | Volatile, sub-second-scope IPC sockets (Linux only) |
29	
30	Tools that follow XDG (most modern ones): nvim, git, mise, starship,
31	zoxide, direnv, bat, eza, atuin, zellij, gh, fd, ripgrep.
32	
33	Tools that **don't** follow XDG (stuck for backwards-compat):
34	- bash (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`)
35	- zsh (`~/.zshrc` — but supports `ZDOTDIR` redirect)
36	- ssh (`~/.ssh/`)
37	- some older tools (`~/.tmux.conf`, `~/.gemrc`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.curlrc`)
38	
39	In this repo: `dot_config/{nvim,git,mise,starship,zoxide,direnv,bat,
40	eza,atuin,zellij,gh,fd,ripgrep,zsh,bash,shell}/` — XDG locations.
41	
42	**Rule — prefer XDG to keep `$HOME` tidy.** When a tool supports *both* a
43	dotfile at `$HOME` root **and** an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the
44	**XDG** copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`), not the `$HOME`-root dotfile. A clean
45	`$HOME` is the goal; only fall back to a root dotfile when the tool genuinely
46	can't read XDG (see A2 — bash, ssh, the classic `~/.gitconfig`, etc.). Confirm
47	the tool's XDG support + lookup order from its docs before choosing the path.
48	
49	> **Watch for "both locations = error" tools.** Some tools search *both* paths
50	> and **abort** if both exist rather than picking one. AeroSpace is the canonical
51	> case: it reads `~/.aerospace.toml` **and** `~/.config/aerospace/aerospace.toml`
52	> and reports an ambiguity error when both are present. So when migrating such a
53	> tool to XDG, also remove the legacy root dotfile — we do this via a gated
54	> `.chezmoiremove` entry (`smart` backup captures it first). See
55	> [`dot_config/aerospace/aerospace.toml`](../../dot_config/aerospace/aerospace.toml)
56	> + the `.aerospace.toml` block in `.chezmoiremove`.
57	
58	### A2. Tool-specific dirs (pre-XDG)
59	
60	OpenSSH lives in `~/.ssh/` with strict 0700 perms. Bash insists on
61	`~/.bashrc` / `~/.bash_profile` at `$HOME`. tmux defaults to
62	`~/.tmux.conf` (newer versions also accept `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`).
63	We follow each tool's actual lookup order rather than fighting it.
64	
65	In this repo: `dot_ssh/`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, `dot_zshrc.tmpl`,
66	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` (also at `$HOME` — git 2.13+ also reads
67	`~/.config/git/config`, but `~/.gitconfig` is the classic canonical).
68	
69	### A3. Platform-specific dirs
70	
71	Some tools use OS-native dirs even on non-XDG:
72	
73	| OS       | Convention                                    |
74	| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
75	| macOS    | `~/Library/Application Support/<App>/`        |
76	| Windows  | `%APPDATA%\<App>\`                            |
77	| Linux    | usually XDG; sometimes `~/.<app>/`            |
78	
79	In this repo: `Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/`
80	(macOS-only chezmoi templates; gated in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` per OS
81	to avoid creating phantom dirs on the other OS).
82	
83	---
84	
85	## B. How modular config is structured
86	
87	### B1. Single canonical file
88	
89	The simplest pattern: one rc file does everything.
90	Examples: `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.tmux.conf`.
91	
92	Pros: easy to read top-to-bottom, no load-order surprises.
93	Cons: grows unwieldy past ~500 lines; merge conflicts when multiple
94	sources contribute.
95	
96	### B2. `.d/` drop-in fragments
97	
98	Old sysadmin pattern from `/etc/` (`/etc/cron.d/`, `/etc/sudoers.d/`,
99	`/etc/profile.d/`, `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`). One canonical file +
100	a `.d/` directory; the tool loops over the dir and sources each
101	fragment alphabetically.
102	
103	User-side examples:
104	- `~/.ssh/config.d/*` (OpenSSH 7.3+; pulled in by `Include config.d/*`
105	  directive in `~/.ssh/config`)
106	- `~/.bashrc.d/*` (RHEL/Rocky/Alma/Fedora skel; their `~/.bashrc`
107	  loops over this dir)
108	- `~/.bash_completion.d/*` (less standard; some completion frameworks)
109	
110	Pros: drop a file → enabled. Each fragment is independent; a package
111	can ship one without modifying the canonical config.
112	Cons: order is glob-sort fragile (most use `NN_` prefixes). Tools
113	that don't natively support `.d/` need a manual loader.
114	
115	In this repo: `dot_ssh/private_config.d/` → `~/.ssh/config.d/*`,
116	included by `~/.ssh/config`. Plus `~/.bashrc.d/*` is sourced as a
117	user backward-compat layer in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` step 11 (NOT where
118	we place chezmoi-managed bash configs — see B3).
119	
120	### B3. Hybrid: XDG location + `.d`-style modular inside
121	
122	When a tool's canonical config doesn't natively support `.d/` but we
123	want the modular benefits: put modular files at the XDG location and
124	write our own loader.
125	
126	In this repo: `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/NN_*.{sh,zsh,bash}` —
127	sourced by a `load_modular_dir` function defined in
128	`dot_zshrc.tmpl` / `dot_bashrc.tmpl` that globs `*.<ext>` and sources
129	in alphabetical order. The `NN_` filename prefix controls load order.
130	
131	Why not just put these in `~/.bashrc.d/`? Because the skel's
132	`~/.bashrc.d` loop (on RHEL) runs from inside the original `~/.bashrc`
133	— after we replace that with our managed bashrc, that loop is gone.
134	Our own bashrc sources `~/.bashrc.d/*` at step 11 (after ble-attach),
135	which is too late for OMB plugin config or pre-init env. So managed
136	configs live in `~/.config/{shell,bash}/` (loaded mid-bashrc), and
137	`~/.bashrc.d/` is reserved for **user-dropped** files only.
138	
139	Full deep-dive: [`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md).
140	
141	### B4. Plugin manager directories
142	
143	When a tool has a plugin manager (oh-my-zsh, oh-my-bash, tpm, lazy.nvim,
144	direnvrc), plugins live in a dedicated dir managed by the framework:
145	
146	- `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/<plugin>/` (OMZ; cloned via
147	  `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
148	- `~/.oh-my-bash/custom/plugins/<plugin>/` (OMB; same pattern)
149	- `~/.tmux/plugins/<plugin>/` (TPM)
150	- `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` + `~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/<plugin>/`
151	  (lazy.nvim — config in XDG_CONFIG_HOME, payloads in XDG_DATA_HOME)
152	
153	We don't fight these — let the framework own its dir, and clone
154	upstream plugins via `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` so chezmoi pulls
155	them weekly.
156	
157	---
158	
159	## C. User customisation layers (override patterns)
160	
161	These are escape hatches — places where users can stash machine-
162	local or experimental config without polluting chezmoi-managed files.
163	
164	### C1. `~/.foorc.local` include (the [include] directive pattern)
165	
166	Used when the canonical config supports an "include another file"
167	directive. The managed file ends with a conditional include of
168	`~/.foorc.local`; the local file is gitignored / chezmoi-ignored.
169	
170	Examples in this repo:
171	- `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` includes `~/.gitconfig.local` (per-machine
172	  `[safe]`, `[credential]`, `[http.proxy]`). Listed in
173	  `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` so chezmoi never tracks it. Silently
174	  no-ops when absent (git's `[include] path = ~/.gitconfig.local`
175	  is forgiving).
176	- `dot_ssh/dot_config` includes `~/.ssh/config.local` similarly.
177	
178	When to use: tool has native include directive AND the canonical
179	config has stable structure that won't break on partial overrides.
180	
181	### C2. `~/.foorc.adhoc` self-sourced tail (our chezmoi-ignored pattern)
182	
183	Used when there's no native include directive — we hand-roll one at
184	the end of the managed rc:
185	
186	```bash
187	# end of dot_zshrc.tmpl / dot_bashrc.tmpl
188	[ -r "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc" ] && . "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc"
189	```
190	
191	Auto-created on first apply with a header comment. Listed in
192	`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Sourced LAST so the user always wins on
193	conflict.
194	
195	When to use: shell rc files where we want a per-machine override
196	without forcing the user to learn chezmoi templates. See `dot_zshrc
197	.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` for the canonical examples.
198	
199	### C3. distro skel conventions (`~/.bash_aliases`, `~/.bashrc.d/*`)
200	
201	Files / dirs that distro `/etc/skel/` configs tell users to populate.
202	Not chezmoi-managed; we just source them for backward-compat so
203	existing user content survives our managed rc taking over.
204	
205	Examples:
206	- `~/.bash_aliases` — Debian / Ubuntu skel sources this; our managed
207	  bashrc step 11 also sources it.
208	- `~/.bashrc.d/*` — RHEL / Rocky / Alma / Fedora skel loops over it;
209	  our managed bashrc step 11 also loops.
210	- `~/.profile` / `~/.bash_profile` — login-shell entry; our
211	  `dot_bash_profile.tmpl` checks for `~/.profile` and sources it
212	  before `~/.bashrc` (with a `grep` guard against double-sourcing).
213	
214	When to use: only for **user-side** legacy compat. Our chezmoi-
215	managed configs DON'T live here.
216	
217	### C4. Secrets files (gitignored / chezmoi-ignored)
218	
219	Per-machine API keys, tokens, proxy URLs — never tracked. Sourced
220	by the managed rc, presence-gated:
221	
222	```bash
223	[ -r "$HOME/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh" ] && . "$HOME/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh"
224	```
225	
226	Listed in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. We also have a baseline-seed
227	pattern via `create_99_local_proxy.zsh` (chezmoi creates it once,
228	then never touches contents).
229	
230	When to use: anything that contains credentials. The
231	[`secrets`](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/encryption/age/) topic
232	in chezmoi docs covers encrypted alternatives if "gitignored" isn't
233	strong enough.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## D. Chezmoi-specific conventions (file prefixes & meta-files)
238	
239	For full mechanics see [`tools/chezmoi-templating.md`](../tools/chezmoi-templating.md)
240	and [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The
241	TL;DR:
242	
243	| Prefix / suffix     | Behaviour                                                   |
244	| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
245	| `dot_X`             | Deploys to `~/.X`                                            |
246	| `private_X`         | Deploys with mode 0600                                       |
247	| `executable_X`      | Deploys with mode 0755 (or +x bit set)                       |
248	| `*.tmpl`            | Templated; rendered at apply time                            |
249	| `modify_X`          | Script that takes current target on stdin, writes new on stdout (jq overlays, etc.) |
250	| `create_X`          | Seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after creation     |
251	| `run_once_before_*` | One-shot pre-apply scripts                                   |
252	| `run_onchange_after_*` | Re-runs on hash change of inlined dependencies            |
253	
254	| Meta-file                         | Purpose                                       |
255	| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
256	| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`              | User config (prompts → data values)            |
257	| `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`             | Source files to skip / OS-conditional gates   |
258	| `.chezmoiremove`                  | Paths to delete from `$HOME` on apply (migrations) |
259	| `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`      | Upstream sources (git clones, file downloads) |
260	| `.chezmoidata*`                   | Static data injected into all templates       |
261	| `.chezmoiscripts/`                | Run-scripts not deployed as files             |
262	
263	---
264	
265	## E. Other related conventions worth knowing
266	
267	### E1. PATH directory conventions
268	
269	| Directory             | Convention | What lives there |
270	| --------------------- | ---------- | ---------------- |
271	| `~/.dotfiles/bin/`    | This repo  | chezmoi-managed user scripts (source: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`) — fleet, sms, mi-router, sesh-preview, x |
272	| `~/bin/`              | Old POSIX  | Legacy / user-placed binaries (transitional; PATH entry will be removed once every host has cleaned up the old `~/bin/*` chezmoi-deployed copies) |
273	| `~/.local/bin/`       | XDG-ish    | Auto-installed CLIs (uv, mise, chezmoi, just, fd, eza, …) |
274	| `~/.cargo/bin/`       | Rust       | cargo-installed binaries |
275	| `~/go/bin/`           | Go         | `go install` targets |
276	| `~/.bun/bin/`         | Bun        | bun runtime + globally-installed JS CLIs |
277	| `~/Library/pnpm/`     | macOS pnpm | pnpm global store |
278	| `/opt/homebrew/bin/`  | macOS brew | Apple Silicon brew |
279	| `/usr/local/bin/`     | macOS brew | Intel brew & legacy `/usr/local` |
280	
281	Order in our `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl` is deliberate:
282	later prepends win, so `$HOME/bin` and `$HOME/.local/bin` end up at
283	the front.
284	
285	### E2. Lock files
286	
287	Lock files pin transitive dep versions. Some are chezmoi-managed,
288	some are gitignored, some are seed-once:
289	
290	| File                                      | Pattern              | Why |
291	| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --- |
292	| `uv.lock`                                 | tracked              | reproducible Python tool installs |
293	| `.chezmoi.toml`                           | gitignored           | output of `chezmoi init`, machine-local |
294	| `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`           | `create_` (seed once) | chezmoi never touches after first apply |
295	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`              | `modify_` (jq merge) | chezmoi-managed AND mergeable |
296	
297	The choice of pattern depends on whether the file should be
298	identical across machines, partly identical, or fully machine-local.
299	
300	### E3. Login vs interactive vs non-interactive shell loading
301	
302	Bash and zsh distinguish three shell modes; each reads different
303	files:
304	
305	| Mode                  | Bash reads                                   | zsh reads                          |
306	| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
307	| Login (TTY/SSH login) | `/etc/profile`, then first of `~/.bash_profile`/`~/.bash_login`/`~/.profile` | `/etc/zprofile`, `~/.zprofile`, `/etc/zlogin`, `~/.zlogin` (and `.zshenv` always) |
308	| Interactive non-login | `/etc/bash.bashrc`, `~/.bashrc`              | `~/.zshenv`, `~/.zshrc`            |
309	| Non-interactive (scripts) | nothing (unless `BASH_ENV` set)         | `~/.zshenv` only                   |
310	
311	Implication: **env vars that need to be available to scripts** must
312	go in `~/.zshenv` (zsh) or be exported via `~/.profile` (bash login
313	chain) — not `~/.zshrc` / `~/.bashrc` (interactive only).
314	
315	In this repo: most env vars live in `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`
316	which gets sourced from BOTH `~/.bashrc` AND `~/.zshrc` — interactive
317	shells only. Things that genuinely need non-interactive scope (PATH
318	for `cron`, `ssh user@host cmd`) belong in `~/.profile` /
319	`~/.zshenv` instead. We accept this tradeoff because: (a) most
320	non-interactive scripts set their own PATH, (b) cron scripts should
321	hardcode tool paths anyway for reproducibility.
322	
323	### E4. Filename-prefix ordering
324	
325	When a `.d/`-style or hybrid loader sorts files alphabetically,
326	filename prefixes encode load order:
327	
328	```
329	dot_config/shell/
330	├── 00_exports.sh.tmpl     ← runs first  (env / PATH)
331	├── 01_starship.sh         ← prompt init (after env)
332	├── 02_legacy_tools.sh     ← legacy PATH additions
333	├── 05_mise.sh             ← runtime manager
334	├── 10_aliases.sh          ← aliases (after env)
335	├── 10_fzf.sh
336	├── 20_zoxide.sh
337	├── 27_thefuck.sh
338	└── 30_direnv.sh           ← runs last
339	```
340	
341	Convention: `00–09` for env / PATH, `10–19` for prompt + tools that
342	depend on env, `20–29` for navigation / utility tools, `30+` for
343	late hooks (direnv, OSC 133, etc). Leave gaps for future inserts —
344	prefer `15_` to inserting between `10_` and `11_`.
345	
346	### E5. Per-OS / per-profile gating in templates
347	
348	When the same source needs different behavior per OS or profile, two
349	patterns:
350	
351	1. **chezmoi template `if`** at template-render time:
352	   ```go
353	   {{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
354	       eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
355	   {{ else -}}
356	       # Linuxbrew path
357	   {{ end -}}
358	   ```
359	
360	2. **runtime detection** at source-time:
361	   ```bash
362	   if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
363	       eval "$(starship init zsh)"
364	   elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
365	       eval "$(starship init bash)"
366	   fi
367	   ```
368	
369	When to use: chezmoi template if the diff is large (whole conditional
370	blocks of config) or if the value is fixed at apply time. Runtime
371	detection if the same file needs to work in different shells (our
372	shared layer) or under different runtime conditions (presence of a
373	binary).
374	
375	Don't double-gate: if a chezmoi template `if` already excludes a
376	branch, the runtime check inside it is dead code. Pick one.
377	
378	---
379	
380	## F. Cross-references
381	
382	- [`tools/chezmoi-templating.md`](../tools/chezmoi-templating.md) —
383	  the chezmoi template language, OS detection, when to use templates
384	  vs static files.
385	- [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md) — full
386	  catalog of `dot_`, `private_`, `executable_`, `modify_`, `create_`
387	  prefix semantics with case studies.
388	- [`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md) — three-tier
389	  shell layout (`dot_config/shell/` vs `dot_config/zsh/` vs
390	  `dot_config/bash/`), migration story, future-shell extension.
391	- [`shells/aliases.md`](../shells/aliases.md) — alias / function
392	  inventory keyed by source file.
393	- [`tools/agent-overlays.md`](../tools/agent-overlays.md) — case
394	  study of `modify_` prefix for jq-based config overlays.
395	- [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) — agent-facing maintenance contract;
396	  cross-file rules (`README.md`, `mkdocs.yml`, `docs/`,
397	  `docs/shells/aliases.md` updates).
398
```

1	# 設定檔慣例 (Config file conventions)
2	
3	!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
4	    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
5	    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
6	    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。
7	
8	本文快速導覽本 repo 採用的 dotfile／設定檔組織模式 (organisation patterns)、
9	各自存在的原因，以及新檔案應放置的位置。
10	
11	這是一份**慣例參考文件 (conventions reference)**，並非 chezmoi 教學——
12	chezmoi 的機制請見 [`tools/chezmoi-templating.md`](../tools/chezmoi-templating.md)
13	與 [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md)；shell 專屬的
14	分層規則請見 [`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md)。
15	
16	---
17	
18	## A. 設定檔放在哪裡 (Where configs live)
19	
20	### A1. XDG Base Directory Specification
21	
22	[freedesktop.org spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html)；
23	現代的預設方案。四個環境變數 (env vars) 將 `$HOME` 切分成依用途標記的子樹：
24	
25	| Env var             | 預設值                  | 內容用途 |
26	| ------------------- | ---------------------- | -------- |
27	| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`  | `~/.config/`           | 使用者設定（90% 的現代工具放這裡） |
28	| `$XDG_DATA_HOME`    | `~/.local/share/`      | 應用資料、工具安裝（mise toolchains、oh-my-zsh、blesh、…） |
29	| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`   | `~/.cache/`            | 可丟棄的快取 (caches)（zsh history search cache、bat cache、…） |
30	| `$XDG_STATE_HOME`   | `~/.local/state/`      | 執行期狀態 (runtime state)；重要性低於 data，較少使用 |
31	| `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`  | `/run/user/$UID/`      | 揮發性、亞秒級範圍的 IPC sockets（僅 Linux） |
32	
33	遵循 XDG 的工具（多數現代工具）：nvim、git、mise、starship、
34	zoxide、direnv、bat、eza、atuin、zellij、gh、fd、ripgrep。
35	
36	**不**遵循 XDG 的工具（為向後相容卡住）：
37	- bash (`~/.bashrc`、`~/.bash_profile`)
38	- zsh (`~/.zshrc`——但支援 `ZDOTDIR` 重導)
39	- ssh (`~/.ssh/`)
40	- 一些較舊的工具 (`~/.tmux.conf`、`~/.gemrc`、`~/.npmrc`、`~/.curlrc`)
41	
42	在本 repo 中：`dot_config/{nvim,git,mise,starship,zoxide,direnv,bat,
43	eza,atuin,zellij,gh,fd,ripgrep,zsh,bash,shell}/`——XDG 位置。
44	
45	### A2. 工具專屬目錄 (Tool-specific dirs, pre-XDG)
46	
47	OpenSSH 位於 `~/.ssh/`，並要求嚴格的 0700 權限。Bash 堅持使用 `$HOME`
48	下的 `~/.bashrc` / `~/.bash_profile`。tmux 預設為 `~/.tmux.conf`
49	（較新版本也接受 `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`）。我們順從各工具實際的查找
50	順序，而非與之對抗。
51	
52	在本 repo 中：`dot_ssh/`、`dot_bashrc.tmpl`、`dot_zshrc.tmpl`、
53	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl`（同樣放在 `$HOME`——git 2.13+ 也讀取
54	`~/.config/git/config`，但 `~/.gitconfig` 是經典的標準位置）。
55	
56	### A3. 平台專屬目錄 (Platform-specific dirs)
57	
58	部分工具即便不採 XDG，也會使用 OS 原生目錄：
59	
60	| OS       | 慣例                                          |
61	| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
62	| macOS    | `~/Library/Application Support/<App>/`        |
63	| Windows  | `%APPDATA%\<App>\`                            |
64	| Linux    | 通常為 XDG；偶爾為 `~/.<app>/`                 |
65	
66	在本 repo 中：`Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/`
67	（僅 macOS 的 chezmoi 模板；在 `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` 中按 OS 條件 gating，
68	避免在另一個 OS 上產生幽靈目錄 (phantom dirs)）。
69	
70	---
71	
72	## B. 模組化設定的組織方式 (How modular config is structured)
73	
74	### B1. 單一標準檔 (Single canonical file)
75	
76	最簡單的模式：一個 rc 檔搞定一切。
77	範例：`~/.gitconfig`、`~/.tmux.conf`。
78	
79	優點：可從上而下閱讀，不會有載入順序的意外。
80	缺點：超過 ~500 行後變得難以管理；多個來源同時貢獻時會發生 merge conflict。
81	
82	### B2. `.d/` drop-in 片段 (drop-in fragments)
83	
84	源自 `/etc/` 的舊式 sysadmin 模式 (`/etc/cron.d/`、`/etc/sudoers.d/`、
85	`/etc/profile.d/`、`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`)。一個標準檔加上一個 `.d/`
86	目錄；工具會掃描該目錄並依字母順序載入每個片段 (fragment)。
87	
88	使用者端範例：
89	- `~/.ssh/config.d/*`（OpenSSH 7.3+；由 `~/.ssh/config` 中的
90	  `Include config.d/*` 指令拉入）
91	- `~/.bashrc.d/*`（RHEL/Rocky/Alma/Fedora skel；其 `~/.bashrc` 會迴圈載入此目錄）
92	- `~/.bash_completion.d/*`（較不標準；某些補全框架使用）
93	
94	優點：丟一個檔進去就啟用。每個片段獨立；套件可不修改標準設定就附帶一份。
95	缺點：順序受 glob 排序左右、易脆 (fragile)（多數採用 `NN_` 前綴）。
96	原生不支援 `.d/` 的工具需要手寫 loader。
97	
98	在本 repo 中：`dot_ssh/private_config.d/` → `~/.ssh/config.d/*`，
99	由 `~/.ssh/config` include 進來。此外 `~/.bashrc.d/*` 在
100	`dot_bashrc.tmpl` 第 11 步以使用者向後相容層 (user backward-compat layer)
101	被 source（**並非**我們放置 chezmoi 管理之 bash 設定的位置——見 B3）。
102	
103	### B3. 混合式：XDG 位置 + `.d` 風格模組化 (Hybrid: XDG location + `.d`-style modular inside)
104	
105	當工具的標準設定檔原生不支援 `.d/`，但我們又想取得模組化的好處時：
106	把模組化檔案放在 XDG 位置，並自行寫一個 loader。
107	
108	在本 repo 中：`dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/NN_*.{sh,zsh,bash}`——
109	由 `dot_zshrc.tmpl` / `dot_bashrc.tmpl` 中定義的 `load_modular_dir` 函式
110	glob `*.<ext>` 並依字母順序 source。`NN_` 檔名前綴控制載入順序。
111	
112	為什麼不直接放在 `~/.bashrc.d/`？因為（在 RHEL 上）skel 的
113	`~/.bashrc.d` 迴圈是從原本的 `~/.bashrc` 內部執行的——當我們將其替換
114	為自管的 bashrc 後，那個迴圈就不存在了。我們自己的 bashrc 在第 11 步
115	（在 ble-attach 之後）才 source `~/.bashrc.d/*`，這對 OMB plugin
116	設定或 pre-init env 來說太晚。所以受管的設定放在
117	`~/.config/{shell,bash}/`（在 bashrc 中段被載入），而 `~/.bashrc.d/`
118	保留給**使用者自行放入**的檔案。
119	
120	完整深入說明：[`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md)。
121	
122	### B4. 套件管理器目錄 (Plugin manager directories)
123	
124	當工具有套件管理器 (plugin manager)（oh-my-zsh、oh-my-bash、tpm、lazy.nvim、
125	direnvrc）時，套件存在框架管理的專屬目錄中：
126	
127	- `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/<plugin>/`（OMZ；透過
128	  `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` clone）
129	- `~/.oh-my-bash/custom/plugins/<plugin>/`（OMB；同樣模式）
130	- `~/.tmux/plugins/<plugin>/`（TPM）
131	- `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` + `~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/<plugin>/`
132	  (lazy.nvim——設定在 XDG_CONFIG_HOME，payload 在 XDG_DATA_HOME)
133	
134	我們不去抗拒它們——讓框架自己管自己的目錄，並透過
135	`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` clone 上游套件，讓 chezmoi 每週自動拉取。
136	
137	---
138	
139	## C. 使用者自訂層 (User customisation layers, override patterns)
140	
141	這些是逃生口 (escape hatches)——讓使用者藏放本機專屬或實驗性設定的位置，
142	而不污染 chezmoi 管理的檔案。
143	
144	### C1. `~/.foorc.local` include（[include] 指令模式）
145	
146	適用於標準設定支援「include 另一個檔案」指令的情況。受管檔案
147	結尾條件性 include `~/.foorc.local`；該本機檔案被 gitignored / chezmoi-ignored。
148	
149	本 repo 範例：
150	- `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` include `~/.gitconfig.local`（per-machine
151	  `[safe]`、`[credential]`、`[http.proxy]`）。列在
152	  `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` 中，所以 chezmoi 不會追蹤它。檔案不存在時
153	  會無聲略過（git 的 `[include] path = ~/.gitconfig.local` 是寬容的）。
154	- `dot_ssh/dot_config` 以類似方式 include `~/.ssh/config.local`。
155	
156	何時使用：當工具具備原生 include 指令，且標準設定有穩定的結構、
157	不會因部分覆寫而壞掉時。
158	
159	### C2. `~/.foorc.adhoc` 自我載入尾段（本 repo chezmoi-ignored 模式）
160	
161	當沒有原生 include 指令時——我們在受管 rc 檔的尾端手動實作一個：
162	
163	```bash
164	# end of dot_zshrc.tmpl / dot_bashrc.tmpl
165	[ -r "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc" ] && . "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc"
166	```
167	
168	第一次 apply 時自動建立，並附上標頭註解。列在 `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` 中。
169	最後 source，因此遇到衝突時使用者永遠勝出。
170	
171	何時使用：希望提供 per-machine 覆寫但又不想強迫使用者學習 chezmoi 模板的
172	shell rc 檔。標準範例見 `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 與 `dot_bashrc.tmpl`。
173	
174	### C3. 發行版 skel 慣例（`~/.bash_aliases`、`~/.bashrc.d/*`）
175	
176	發行版 `/etc/skel/` 設定告訴使用者去填的檔案／目錄。並非 chezmoi 管理；
177	我們只是 source 它們以保持向後相容，讓既有的使用者內容能在我們接管 rc
178	之後仍然存活。
179	
180	範例：
181	- `~/.bash_aliases`——Debian / Ubuntu skel 會 source 這個；我們受管的
182	  bashrc 在第 11 步也會 source。
183	- `~/.bashrc.d/*`——RHEL / Rocky / Alma / Fedora skel 會迴圈載入；
184	  我們受管的 bashrc 第 11 步也會迴圈載入。
185	- `~/.profile` / `~/.bash_profile`——login shell 入口；我們的
186	  `dot_bash_profile.tmpl` 會檢查 `~/.profile` 並在 `~/.bashrc` 之前
187	  source 它（並透過 `grep` 防止 double-sourcing）。
188	
189	何時使用：僅用於**使用者端**的 legacy 相容性。我們 chezmoi 管理的設定
190	**不**放在這裡。
191	
192	### C4. 機密檔 (Secrets files, gitignored / chezmoi-ignored)
193	
194	Per-machine 的 API keys、tokens、proxy URLs——絕不追蹤。由受管 rc source，
195	並做存在性檢查 (presence-gated)：
196	
197	```bash
198	[ -r "$HOME/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh" ] && . "$HOME/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh"
199	```
200	
201	列在 `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` 中。我們也透過 `create_99_local_proxy.zsh`
202	提供 baseline-seed 模式（chezmoi 建立一次後，永不再動內容）。
203	
204	何時使用：任何包含憑證的內容。若「gitignored」還不夠強，chezmoi 文件中的
205	[`secrets`](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/encryption/age/) 主題涵蓋了
206	加密替代方案。
207	
208	---
209	
210	## D. chezmoi 專屬慣例（檔名前綴與 meta 檔）(Chezmoi-specific conventions)
211	
212	完整機制請見 [`tools/chezmoi-templating.md`](../tools/chezmoi-templating.md)
213	與 [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md)。TL;DR：
214	
215	| 前綴 / 後綴          | 行為                                                         |
216	| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
217	| `dot_X`             | 部署為 `~/.X`                                                |
218	| `private_X`         | 以 mode 0600 部署                                            |
219	| `executable_X`      | 以 mode 0755 部署（或設定 +x bit）                            |
220	| `*.tmpl`            | 模板化；apply 時渲染                                         |
221	| `modify_X`          | 一支腳本，從 stdin 接收當前 target，並把新內容寫到 stdout（jq overlay 等） |
222	| `create_X`          | 種子一次；建立後 chezmoi 永不再動內容                          |
223	| `run_once_before_*` | 一次性的 pre-apply 腳本                                      |
224	| `run_onchange_after_*` | 當 inline 依賴的 hash 變動時重新執行                       |
225	
226	| Meta 檔                            | 用途                                          |
227	| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
228	| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`              | 使用者設定（提示 → data 值）                   |
229	| `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`             | 要略過 / 按 OS 條件 gating 的來源檔            |
230	| `.chezmoiremove`                  | apply 時要從 `$HOME` 刪除的路徑（用於遷移）    |
231	| `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`      | 上游來源（git clone、檔案下載）                |
232	| `.chezmoidata*`                   | 注入到所有模板的靜態資料                       |
233	| `.chezmoiscripts/`                | 不會以檔案形式部署的 run-scripts               |
234	
235	---
236	
237	## E. 其他值得知道的相關慣例 (Other related conventions worth knowing)
238	
239	### E1. PATH 目錄慣例 (PATH directory conventions)
240	
241	| 目錄                  | 慣例       | 內容 |
242	| --------------------- | ---------- | ---- |
243	| `~/bin/`              | 老式 POSIX | 使用者撰寫的 shell 腳本（`dot_bin/` 中有幾個） |
244	| `~/.local/bin/`       | XDG-ish    | 自動安裝的 CLI（uv、mise、chezmoi、just、fd、eza、…） |
245	| `~/.cargo/bin/`       | Rust       | cargo 安裝的 binary |
246	| `~/go/bin/`           | Go         | `go install` 的 target |
247	| `~/.bun/bin/`         | Bun        | bun runtime + 全域安裝的 JS CLI |
248	| `~/Library/pnpm/`     | macOS pnpm | pnpm 全域 store |
249	| `/opt/homebrew/bin/`  | macOS brew | Apple Silicon brew |
250	| `/usr/local/bin/`     | macOS brew | Intel brew 與舊式 `/usr/local` |
251	
252	我們在 `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl` 中的順序是刻意的：
253	較晚 prepend 者勝出，因此 `$HOME/bin` 與 `$HOME/.local/bin` 最終排在最前面。
254	
255	### E2. Lock 檔 (Lock files)
256	
257	Lock 檔釘住傳遞性依賴 (transitive dep) 的版本。有些由 chezmoi 管理，
258	有些被 gitignored，有些是 seed-once：
259	
260	| 檔案                                       | 模式                  | 原因 |
261	| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --- |
262	| `uv.lock`                                 | 追蹤                 | 可重現的 Python 工具安裝 |
263	| `.chezmoi.toml`                           | gitignored           | `chezmoi init` 的輸出，machine-local |
264	| `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`           | `create_`（種子一次） | 首次 apply 後 chezmoi 永不再動 |
265	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`              | `modify_`（jq 合併）  | chezmoi 管理且可合併 |
266	
267	模式選擇取決於該檔案應該跨機器完全相同、部分相同，或完全 machine-local。
268	
269	### E3. Login、interactive、non-interactive shell 載入差異
270	
271	Bash 與 zsh 區分三種 shell 模式；每種讀取不同的檔案：
272	
273	| 模式                  | Bash 讀取                                     | zsh 讀取                            |
274	| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
275	| Login（TTY/SSH 登入） | `/etc/profile`，然後 `~/.bash_profile`/`~/.bash_login`/`~/.profile` 中第一個存在者 | `/etc/zprofile`、`~/.zprofile`、`/etc/zlogin`、`~/.zlogin`（以及永遠讀取的 `.zshenv`） |
276	| Interactive non-login | `/etc/bash.bashrc`、`~/.bashrc`              | `~/.zshenv`、`~/.zshrc`             |
277	| Non-interactive（腳本） | 不讀任何檔（除非設定 `BASH_ENV`）           | 僅 `~/.zshenv`                     |
278	
279	含意：**腳本需要使用的環境變數**必須放在 `~/.zshenv`（zsh）或透過
280	`~/.profile`（bash login chain）export——不是 `~/.zshrc` / `~/.bashrc`
281	（僅 interactive）。
282	
283	在本 repo 中：多數環境變數放在 `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`，
284	從 `~/.bashrc` 與 `~/.zshrc` 兩邊都被 source——僅限 interactive shell。
285	真正需要 non-interactive scope 的東西（`cron` 的 PATH、
286	`ssh user@host cmd`）應該放在 `~/.profile` / `~/.zshenv`。我們接受
287	這個取捨，因為：(a) 多數 non-interactive 腳本會自行設定 PATH；(b)
288	cron 腳本本來就應該為了可重現性而 hardcode 工具路徑。
289	
290	### E4. 檔名前綴排序 (Filename-prefix ordering)
291	
292	當 `.d/` 風格或 hybrid loader 依字母順序排列檔案時，檔名前綴即編碼了
293	載入順序：
294	
295	```
296	dot_config/shell/
297	├── 00_exports.sh.tmpl     ← 最先執行  (env / PATH)
298	├── 01_starship.sh         ← prompt 初始化（在 env 之後）
299	├── 02_legacy_tools.sh     ← legacy PATH 增補
300	├── 05_mise.sh             ← runtime manager
301	├── 10_aliases.sh          ← aliases（在 env 之後）
302	├── 10_fzf.sh
303	├── 20_zoxide.sh
304	├── 27_thefuck.sh
305	└── 30_direnv.sh           ← 最後執行
306	```
307	
308	慣例：`00–09` 為 env / PATH；`10–19` 為 prompt 與依賴 env 的工具；
309	`20–29` 為導航／實用工具；`30+` 為晚期 hook（direnv、OSC 133 等）。
310	編號之間留間隔以利日後插入——優先用 `15_`，而非硬塞在 `10_` 與 `11_` 之間。
311	
312	### E5. 模板中的 per-OS / per-profile 條件控制 (Per-OS / per-profile gating in templates)
313	
314	當同一份來源在不同 OS 或 profile 下需要不同行為時，有兩種模式：
315	
316	1. **chezmoi 模板 `if`**（在模板渲染時）：
317	   ```go
318	   {{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
319	       eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
320	   {{ else -}}
321	       # Linuxbrew path
322	   {{ end -}}
323	   ```
324	
325	2. **執行時偵測 (runtime detection)**（在 source 時）：
326	   ```bash
327	   if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
328	       eval "$(starship init zsh)"
329	   elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
330	       eval "$(starship init bash)"
331	   fi
332	   ```
333	
334	何時使用：若差異很大（整段條件式設定區塊）或值在 apply 時即固定，採用
335	chezmoi 模板。若同一份檔案需在不同 shell（我們的 shared 層）或不同
336	runtime 條件（某 binary 是否存在）下都要能跑，採用 runtime detection。
337	
338	不要 double-gate：若 chezmoi 模板的 `if` 已排除某 branch，該 branch 內
339	的 runtime 檢查就是死碼 (dead code)。擇一即可。
340

350	
351	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
352	
353	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
354	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
355	
356	## Prerequisites
357	
358	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
359	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
360

368	        MISE[mise]

387	        CASKS[GUI Apps]
388	        MAS[App Store]
389	    end
390	
391	    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible

393	    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM

399	## Quick Setup
400	
401	```bash
402	# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
403	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
404	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
405	```
406	
407	This automatically:
408	
409	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
410	2. Deploys all config files
411	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
412	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` enabled)
413	
414	### Optional Components
415	
416	During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
417	
418	| Option | Default | Description |
419	|--------|---------|-------------|
420	| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, etc. |
421	| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
422	| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, litellm, sqlit-tui, etc.) |
423	| `installBrewApps` | false | GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (casks, mas) |
424	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
425	
426	To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
427	
428	## What You Get
429	
430	### Config Files
431	
432	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
433	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
434	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
435	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
436	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
437	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
438	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config
439	- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
440	- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins
441	- `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
442	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
443	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
444	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI completion + SSH agent socket auto-detection
445	- `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas)
446	
447	### Tools (via ansible)
448	
449	- **Base**: git, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
450	- **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
451	- **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
452	- **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, SpecStory, Happy, OpenChamber
453	- **Bitwarden** (optional): Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) via npm, Desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, cask on macOS) on desktop profiles, with zsh completion and SSH agent auto-detection
454	- **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
455	- **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager)
456	- **GUI Apps** (macOS): terminals, editors, browsers, utilities via Brewfile
457	
458	### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
459	- **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
460	- **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
461	- **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (ensures latest versions)
462	- **Dev tools**: bat, eza, git-delta, tldr, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, tmux+tpm, zellij, btop, htop
463	- **NerdFonts**: Hack Nerd Font for terminal emulators

496	# Bitwarden SSH Agent
497	
498	Use the Bitwarden desktop app as your SSH agent so private keys never leave the vault.
499	
500	- **Official docs**: <https://bitwarden.com/help/ssh-agent/>
501	- **Requires**: Bitwarden desktop >= 2025.1.2, SSH agent enabled in **Settings > Enable SSH agent**
502	
503	## 0. Install Bitwarden Desktop
504	
505	### Automated (via this repo)
506	
507	When `installBitwarden` is enabled during `chezmoi init`, the ansible bitwarden role automatically installs:
508	- **CLI** (`bw`): via npm on all profiles
509	- **Desktop app**: on desktop profiles only (`ubuntu_desktop`, `macos`, `macos_intel`)
510	  - **macOS**: via Homebrew Cask (`brew install --cask bitwarden`)
511	  - **Ubuntu**: via Snap (primary) or `.deb` download (fallback)
512	
513	```bash
514	# Enable during chezmoi init (if not already)
515	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "Install Bitwarden CLI" prompt
516	
517	# Or run the bitwarden role manually with desktop install
518	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --tags bitwarden --extra-vars "bitwarden_install_desktop=true"
519	```
520	
521	### Manual
522	
523	If you prefer to install manually or are on `ubuntu_server`:
524	- **macOS**: `brew install --cask bitwarden`
525	- **Ubuntu (snap)**: `sudo snap install bitwarden`
526	- **Ubuntu (.deb)**: Download from [vault.bitwarden.com](https://vault.bitwarden.com/download/?app=desktop&platform=linux&variant=deb)
527	- **Flatpak**: `flatpak install flathub com.bitwarden.desktop`
528	
529	## How It Works
530	
531	```
532	┌──────────────┐     SSH_AUTH_SOCK      ┌───────────────────┐
533	│  ssh / git   │ ───────────────────▶   │  Bitwarden Agent  │
534	│  (any CLI)   │                        │  (desktop app)    │
535	└──────────────┘                        └───────────────────┘
536	                                              │
537	                                              ▼
538	                                        Vault (encrypted)
539	                                        ├─ SSH: ssh_key_1
540	                                        ├─ SSH: ssh_key_2
541	                                        └─ SSH: ssh_key_3
542	```
543	
544	When an SSH client needs a key, it talks to whichever agent `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` points to.
545	Bitwarden creates a Unix socket file; pointing `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` there makes Bitwarden the agent.
546	The desktop app prompts you to authorize each key usage (configurable under Settings).
547	
548	## 1. Import Keys Into Bitwarden
549	
550	### Via the desktop app
551	
552	1. Open Bitwarden desktop, click **New > SSH key**.
553	2. Paste your private key (OpenSSH or PKCS#8 format) using **Import key from clipboard**.
554	3. The public key and fingerprint are derived automatically.
555	
556	### Via the CLI script
557	
558	This repo includes an import script (see [import_ssh_to_bw.sh docs](../scripts/import_ssh_to_bw.sh.md)):
559	
560	```bash
561	# Interactive -- pick which keys to import
562	ssh-to-bitwarden
563	
564	# Import all keys from ~/.ssh
565	ssh-to-bitwarden --all
566	
567	# Preview only
568	ssh-to-bitwarden --dry-run
569	```
570	
571	## 2. Configure SSH_AUTH_SOCK
572	
573	The socket path depends on how Bitwarden was installed:
574	
575	| Installation   | macOS socket path                                                                         | Linux socket path                                                       |
576	|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
577	| `.dmg`         | `~/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`                                                             | --                                                                      |
578	| Mac App Store  | `~/Library/Containers/com.bitwarden.desktop/Data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`               | --                                                                      |
579	| Native / .deb  | --                                                                                        | `~/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`                                           |
580	| Snap           | --                                                                                        | `~/snap/bitwarden/current/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`                    |
581	| Flatpak        | --                                                                                        | `~/.var/app/com.bitwarden.desktop/data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`       |
582	
583	This repo auto-detects the socket in `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh`.
584	It tries each candidate path in order and exports `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` for the first socket that exists.
585	No manual shell configuration is needed if you use the managed zsh config.
586	
587	## 3. Verify
588	
589	```bash
590	# List keys the agent knows about
591	ssh-add -l
592	
593	# Expected output (example):
594	# 3072 SHA256:S93TIv0W2E1B...  SSH: ssh_key_1 (RSA)
595	# 3072 SHA256:B7ZcVqELH0RQ...  SSH: ssh_key_2 (RSA)
596	# 3072 SHA256:i+mZs1/
597	... (truncated)
598	```

of failed hosts. Inventory file is seeded once by chezmoi as a
`create_private_` template, so your edits are never overwritten.

`fleet-status` is the recommended pre-apply gate — it predicts what `fleet-apply`
would do per host (`up-to-date` / `behind` / `drift` / `busy` /
`toml-mismatch` / `not-init` / `unreachable` / ...) without changing
anything, and prints actionable hints for each non-green state. See

1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
17	#
18	# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).
20	
21	[metadata]
22	name = "ssh-config"
23	description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
24	requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]
25	
26	[source]
27	# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '

# Plan: smarter "Local SSH config" step in `ssh-setup-remote`

## Context

`ssh-setup-remote` (`dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`, "Step 3", lines 187–248) currently
**always appends** a fresh `Host` block to the chosen config file. That is wrong for the
common case the user just hit: running `ssh-setup-remote ts_mac` where `ts_mac` is **already**
a configured Host (which is exactly why `ssh-copy-id ts_mac` resolved to `100.100.100.100`).
Appending a second `Host ts_mac` block produces a confusing duplicate.

We want two clean modes:

1. **Adhoc new host** (`user@ip`): one-step — create a Host alias + write the block
   (to `~/.ssh/config` or `~/.ssh/config.d/host_<alias>`). (≈ current behavior, refined.)
2. **Existing host**: the alias already exists but had no key; *add* `IdentityFile` (and
   optionally `IdentitiesOnly yes`) **into the existing block, in whichever file it lives**,
   instead of appending a duplicate.

Crucially the config may be split: `~/.ssh/config` is an entry point that
`Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (repo default). Finding an existing Host must **recursively follow
`Include` directives** to land on the right file. (Note: on this machine the live
`~/.ssh/config` has no `Include` line yet `config.d/` exists — see open question 3.)

## Approach (to finalize after questions)

Rework Step 3 of `dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`:

1. **Resolve effective config files** by following `Include` from `~/.ssh/config` recursively
   (glob expansion relative to `~/.ssh/`, `~`/absolute paths, depth+loop guard).
2. **Detect** a `Host` stanza whose patterns contain the target alias (exact token, skip
   wildcards) across those files.
3. **Branch**:
   - *Existing* → show the matched file + block; offer to insert `IdentityFile <key>`
     (+ optional `IdentitiesOnly yes`) into that block, matching its indentation; idempotent
     (skip if the exact key is already present); handle a pre-existing IdentityFile per Q2.
     Edit in place via temp file + `mv`, then `chmod 600`.
   - *New* → current append flow (alias/hostname/user/IdentitiesOnly prompts; `config` vs
     `config.d/host_<alias>`; confirm; append).
4. Mechanism per Q1.

## Mirror updates (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)
- `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md` + `.zh-TW.md`: update Step 5 description; fix
  stale source path `~/.config/zsh/tools/96_ssh_setup.zsh` → `~/.config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`.
- `docs/shells/aliases.md`: add the missing `ssh-setup-remote` row.

# Plan: smarter "Local SSH config" step in `ssh-setup-remote`

## Context

`ssh-setup-remote` (`dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`, "Step 3: Local SSH config",
lines 187–248) currently **always appends** a fresh `Host` block to the chosen config file.
That is wrong for the case the user just hit: running `ssh-setup-remote ts_mac` where `ts_mac`
is **already** a configured Host (that is exactly why `ssh-copy-id ts_mac` reached
`100.100.100.100`). Appending a second `Host ts_mac` block produces a confusing duplicate, and
the new `IdentityFile` may not even take effect (first-match-wins per key).

We want the wizard to recognize two situations and do the right thing automatically:

1. **Adhoc new host** (`user@ip`): one-step — create a Host alias + write the block. (≈ current
   behavior, refined.)
2. **Existing host**: alias already exists but had no key configured; *add* `IdentityFile`
   (+ optional `IdentitiesOnly yes`) **into the existing block, in whichever file it lives** —
   not a duplicate stanza.

The config can be split: managed `~/.ssh/config` is an entry point that `Include
~/.ssh/config.d/*`. Locating an existing Host must **recursively follow `Include` directives**
(glob, `~`/relative/absolute). On *this* machine the live `~/.ssh/config` is the user's
pre-existing hand-curated file with **no `Include` line**, yet `~/.ssh/config.d/` exists — so
drop-ins here currently do not load (handled below).

### Decisions (confirmed)
- **Mechanism**: inline `python3` heredoc helper for parse/find/edit; shell keeps all
  interactive prompts. Fall back to current append-only flow if `python3` is absent.
- **Existing IdentityFile present**: show the block, prompt `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip`.
- **config.d drop-in but no `Include` in `~/.ssh/config`**: detect and offer to add
  `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*`.

## Implementation

### 1. New shell helper `_ssh_cfg_py()` in `dot_config/shell/96_ssh_setup.sh`

One POSIX-source-safe function wrapping a single `python3 - "$@" <<'PY' … PY` heredoc with a
subcommand dispatch (keeps all Include-resolution logic in one place). Returns 127 if `python3`
is missing so callers can fall back.

Python CLI (root = `$HOME/.ssh/config`, ssh_dir = its parent):
- `resolve_includes(start)` — recursive walk from `~/.ssh/config`; for each non-comment
  `Include` line, split patterns, `os.path.expanduser`, make relative patterns relative to
  `ssh_dir`, `glob.glob`, recurse; `seen` set guards loops; returns ordered file list. Reuses the
  pattern already proven in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py:_detect_ssh` but made recursive.
- `find <alias>` — scan resolved files for a `Host` line whose tokens contain `alias` as an
  exact token (skip `*?!` wildcard/negation patterns, matching the awk in
  `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml`). On hit, print machine-readable
  `key=value` lines for the shell: `found=1`, `file=…`, `has_identityfile=0|1`,
  `identityfile=…`, `key_present=0|1` (idempotency: exact `$key_path` already in block), plus
  the block text (for display). Exit non-zero / `found=0` when not found.
- `insert <file> <alias> <key> <action>` — rewrite the matched block: `action` ∈
  `insert` (no existing IdentityFile), `replace`, `add`. Indentation copied from the block's
  existing indented lines (fallback 4 spaces). Optional trailing `--identities-only` appends
  `IdentitiesOnly yes` if absent. Atomic write: temp file in same dir → `os.replace` →
  reapply `0o600`.
- `ensure-include` / `add-include` — report whether `resolve_includes` reaches
  `~/.ssh/config.d/`; if not, `add-include` prepends `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (with a
  comment) near the top of `~/.ssh/config`, matching `dot_ssh/create_private_config` layout
  (Include-at-top so drop-ins are visible; note first-match-wins ordering).

### 2. Rework "Step 3" (lines 187–248) of `ssh-setup-remote`

Replace the unconditional append with:

1. Pick the lookup alias (default `$remote_host`).
2. `_ssh_cfg_py find "$alias"`:
   - **rc 127** → fall back to the existing append flow unchanged.
   - **found=1 (Mode B — existing)**: print "Host `$alias` already configured in `<file>`" +
     the block. If `key_present` → report "already has this key", skip. Else if
     `has_identityfile` → prompt `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip`; map to `insert` action.
     Offer `IdentitiesOnly yes` if missing. Call `_ssh_cfg_py insert …`. Validate with
     `ssh -G "$alias"`.
   - **found=0 (Mode A — new)**: keep current prompts (alias/hostname/user/IdentitiesOnly,
     `~/.ssh/config` vs `~/.ssh/config.d/host_<alias>`, confirm, append). After writing to
     `config.d/`, run `_ssh_cfg_py ensure-include`; if it can't be reached, offer
     `_ssh_cfg_py add-include`.
3. Final "Test with: ssh `<alias>`" line unchanged (`${host_alias:-$target}`).

Keep everything POSIX-source-safe (file is in shared `dot_config/shell/`; both shells source
it). `[[ … =~ ]]` is already used in this file and works in zsh+bash.

## Mirror updates (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules)

  `key=value` lines for the shell: `found=1`, `file=…`, `has_identityfile=0|1`,
  `identityfile=…`, `key_present=0|1` (idempotency: exact `$key_path` already in block), plus
  the block text (for display). Exit non-zero / `found=0` when not found.
- `insert <file> <alias> <key> <action>` — rewrite the matched block: `action` ∈
  `insert` (no existing IdentityFile), `replace`, `add`. Indentation copied from the block's
  existing indented lines (fallback 4 spaces). Optional trailing `--identities-only` appends
  `IdentitiesOnly yes` if absent. Atomic write: temp file in same dir → `os.replace` →
  reapply `0o600`.
- `ensure-include` / `add-include` — report whether `resolve_includes` reaches
  `~/.ssh/config.d/`; if not, `add-include` prepends `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` (with a
  comment) near the top of `~/.ssh/config`, matching `dot_ssh/create_private_config` layout
  (Include-at-top so drop-ins are visible; note first-match-wins ordering).

### 2. Rework "Step 3" (lines 187–248) of `ssh-setup-remote`

Replace the unconditional append with:

1. Pick the lookup alias (default `$remote_host`).
2. `_ssh_cfg_py find "$alias"`:
   - **rc 127** → fall back to the existing append flow unchanged.
   - **found=1 (Mode B — existing)**: print "Host `$alias` already configured in `<file>`" +
     the block. If `key_present` → report "already has this key", skip. Else if
     `has_identityfile` → prompt `[r]eplace / [a]dd another / [s]kip`; map to `insert` action.
     Offer `IdentitiesOnly yes` if missing. Call `_ssh_cfg_py insert …`. Validate with
     `ssh -G "$alias"`.
   - **found=0 (Mode A — new)**: keep current prompts (alias/hostname/user/IdentitiesOnly,
     `~/.ssh/config` vs `~/.ssh/config.d/host_<alias>`, confirm, append). After writing to
     `config.d/`, run `_ssh_cfg_py ensure-include`; if it can't be reached, offer
     `_ssh_cfg_py add-include`.
3. Final "Test with: ssh `<alias>`" line unchanged (`${host_alias:-$target}`).

Keep everything POSIX-source-safe (file is in shared `dot_config/shell/`; both shells source
it). `[[ … =~ ]]` is already used in this file and works in zsh+bash.

## Automation: `ssh-setup-remote`

This repo includes a shell function that walks through all the steps above interactively:

```bash
ssh-setup-remote user@hostname
```

It will prompt you to:

1. **Select or create** an SSH key (algorithm, name, passphrase)
2. **ssh-copy-id** the public key to enable passwordless login
3. **Copy the key pair** to the remote (optional, for GitHub access)
4. **Add GitHub SSH config** on the remote (optional)
5. **Add a host alias** to your local `~/.ssh/config` (with `IdentitiesOnly` option)

Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/96_ssh_setup.zsh`

## Troubleshooting

### Remote Host Identification Has Changed

If you see `WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!` when connecting, the server's host key no longer matches what's stored in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. This commonly happens after reinstalling the OS or reprovisioning a server at the same IP.
